string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is China’s capital and one of the country’s four municipalities directly administered by the central government. Its long history is visible in places such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and sections of the Great Wall. Beijing is also a modern centre for national government, education, research and culture. The city hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics, making it the first city to host both editions. Its historic central axis was added to UNESCO’s World Heritage List in 2024.

Shanghai is a major port and international commercial centre on China’s east coast, where the Huangpu River meets the Yangtze River Delta. Its historic Bund waterfront faces the modern skyline of Pudong, including the Shanghai Tower. The city’s architecture reflects several periods of Chinese and international history, while its neighbourhoods, museums and performing arts venues contribute to a lively cultural scene. Shanghai is also known for its extensive metro system and as a gateway for trade, finance, technology and travel.

Chongqing is a large municipality in southwest China, set where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet. Its steep terrain, river scenery and dense urban districts have earned it a reputation as a mountain city. Chongqing is an important inland transport and manufacturing hub and forms a key part of the Yangtze River Economic Belt. Visitors often explore the Dazu Rock Carvings, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and take river journeys through the Three Gorges region. The municipality also has a distinctive food culture, especially its spicy hotpot.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China beside the Bohai Sea and close to Beijing. It developed as an important port and trading city, and its Haihe River waterfront connects many historic districts. The city combines traditional Chinese landmarks, including the Tianjin Ancient Culture Street area, with European-influenced buildings and modern development. Tianjin is a major centre for shipping, manufacturing, finance and education. Its port is among China’s busiest, supporting commerce across northern China and international maritime routes. The city is also known for its distinctive local cuisine.
